correction.text: "spread across the arid coastal regions of the Atacama Desert from Ilo, southern Peru to Antofagasta in northern Chile"; core "the Chilean Arica-Camarones region"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "c. 7000 - c. 1500 BCE", range Atacama Desert; "lasted from 9,100 to 3,500 years BP (7,000 to 1,500 BCE)", "inhabiting the Pacific coastal region of current northern Chile and southern Peru". The dossier starts at the project floor (the culture begins about 1,000 years earlier). Five 70 km discs round Ilo, Arica, Iquique, Tocopilla and Antofagasta (158 land cells; Tocopilla added by the xx-01-c reviewer to close the 240 km gap between Iquique and Antofagasta) stand for the coastal strip; the page gives no area or site count.

region.text: "spread across the arid coastal regions of the Atacama Desert from Ilo, southern Peru to Antofagasta in northern Chile"; core "the Chilean Arica-Camarones region"

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): Chinchorro fishers already hold the Atacama coast from Ilo to Antofagasta. "was a preceramic culture that lasted from 9,100 to 3,500 years BP (7,000 to 1,500 BCE)"; "The Chinchorro mummies go back to 9,000 years Before Present, or 7,000 BC". The culture begins before the floor; the strip of discs is the dossier's reading of "from Ilo, southern Peru to Antofagasta in northern Chile".

region.text: "spread across the arid coastal regions of the Atacama Desert from Ilo, southern Peru to Antofagasta in northern Chile"; core "the Chilean Arica-Camarones region"

ledger.note: 1500 BCE: the Chinchorro culture ends. "The end of the Chinchorro culture is set around 3500 BP"; later groups under Andean influence "no longer mummified their dead" and took up agriculture "c. 3,000 BP"; the Wankarani is the infobox successor but is a highland culture, so the coast passes to nobody.

certainty.note: A coastal strip with no recorded border; the inland edge is the desert.

sources.title: Chinchorro culture
sources.note: Infobox c. 7000 - c. 1500 BCE, Atacama Desert; Ilo to Antofagasta, core Arica-Camarones; end around 3500 BP; Azapa phase; Wankarani.

notes: Chinchorro culture, Atacama coast. The culture begins c. 7000 BCE (page), before the project floor of 6000 BCE, so the dossier starts at the floor with the extent the page gives for the whole culture. The page gives dates for the mummification styles (black to red c. 2000 BC) and for Andean influence from c. 4,000 BP but no change of extent, so there are no further events. Wankarani (infobox successor) is Bolivian highland and has no dossier here.
